queue.brief: One-sided deals — where all activity is outbound and the prospect has gone quiet — sit in pipelines for months looking alive while they're actually dead. This post shows how to identify them in monday.com before they distort your forecast.

H2 sections: What a one-sided deal looks like in a monday.com CRM / Why these deals are more dangerous to forecast accuracy than openly lost ones / How to use activity columns and last-contact dates to identify one-sided patterns / The difference between a slow deal and a dead one — and how to tell them apart / How to run a re-engagement check on flagged deals before writing them off / When to close them out and how to do it cleanly without distorting your data. Real-world example: a B2B services firm with 40 open deals in monday.com where 14 have had zero inbound activity logged in 45-plus days — showing how to filter, sort, and review those 14 to determine which are genuinely in progress and which have been one-sided for so long they should be formally disqualified.

queue.brief: Bad forecast numbers in monday.com are rarely caused by missing deal values — they're caused by deal values that were entered inconsistently and never corrected. This post shows the five most common data entry mistakes and exactly how to find and fix them.
